questions.text: Who was the first man created by God according to the Bible?
questions.explanation: Adam was the first man created by God (Genesis 2:7).

questions.text: In which garden were Adam and Eve placed by God?
questions.explanation: God placed Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden (Genesis 2:8).

questions.text: What did Adam and Eve eat that God had forbidden?
options: Fruit from the tree of knowledge
questions.explanation: They ate the forbidden fruit from the tree of knowledge of good and evil (Genesis 3:6).

questions.text: Who tempted Eve in the Garden of Eden?
questions.explanation: The serpent tempted Eve to eat the forbidden fruit (Genesis 3:1).

questions.text: Why was Noah saved from the great flood?
questions.explanation: Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord because he was a righteous man (Genesis 6:8-9).

questions.text: How many days and nights did the rain fall during the flood?
questions.explanation: It rained for forty days and forty nights (Genesis 7:12).

questions.text: Which bird did Noah first send out from the ark?
questions.explanation: Noah first sent out a raven from the ark (Genesis 8:7).

questions.text: What sign did God give as a covenant with Noah after the flood?
questions.explanation: God set a rainbow in the sky as a sign of His covenant with Noah (Genesis 9:13).

questions.text: Who was the son of Abraham offered as a sacrifice to God?
questions.explanation: God tested Abraham by asking him to sacrifice his son Isaac (Genesis 22:2).

questions.text: What new name was given to Jacob after he wrestled with God?
questions.explanation: Jacob was renamed Israel after wrestling with God (Genesis 32:28).

questions.text: How many plagues did God send upon Egypt?
questions.explanation: God sent ten plagues upon Egypt (Exodus 7-12).

questions.text: From what natural object did God call Moses to lead Israel?
questions.explanation: God spoke to Moses from a burning bush (Exodus 3:2).

questions.text: Through which sea did God part for the Israelites to cross?
questions.explanation: God parted the Red Sea so the Israelites could cross on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22).

questions.text: What did God provide for the Israelites to eat in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: God sent manna from heaven and quails as food in the wilderness (Exodus 16:4, 13).

questions.text: On which mountain did Moses receive the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation: Moses received the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:20).

questions.text: How many tablets of the covenant did Moses bring down from the mountain?
questions.explanation: God wrote the commandments on two tablets of stone (Exodus 31:18).

questions.text: What golden object did the Israelites make while Moses was on the mountain?
questions.explanation: The people made a golden calf idol while Moses was on Mount Sinai (Exodus 32:4).

questions.text: Who was the first judge of Israel after Joshua?
questions.explanation: Othniel was the first judge of Israel (Judges 3:9).

questions.text: Which judge of Israel had his strength from his long hair?
questions.explanation: Samson's strength was connected to his Nazirite vow and his long hair (Judges 16:17).

questions.text: How did Samson meet his death according to the Bible?
options: By pulling down the temple pillars
questions.explanation: Samson pulled down the pillars of the Philistine temple, killing himself and his enemies (Judges 16:30).

questions.text: Who betrayed Samson to the Philistines?
questions.explanation: Delilah betrayed Samson after discovering the secret of his strength (Judges 16:18).

questions.text: Which female judge led Israel to victory over the Canaanites?
questions.explanation: Deborah was a prophetess and judge who led Israel to victory (Judges 4:4-9).

questions.text: What did Gideon use to defeat the Midianites?
questions.explanation: Gideon's 300 men used trumpets, torches, and empty jars to confuse and defeat the Midianites (Judges 7:16-20).

questions.text: How many men did Gideon select for his final battle force?
questions.explanation: God reduced Gideon's army to 300 men so Israel would know the victory was from God (Judges 7:7).

questions.text: Which book of the Bible tells the story of Ruth?
questions.explanation: The Book of Ruth tells the story of Ruth's loyalty and her journey to Bethlehem.

questions.text: Whose mother prayed for a child and received Samuel?
questions.explanation: Hannah prayed earnestly for a son and God answered her prayer, giving her Samuel (1 Samuel 1:20).

questions.text: Who anointed Saul as the first king of Israel?
questions.explanation: Samuel anointed Saul as the first king of Israel at God's command (1 Samuel 10:1).

questions.text: Why did God reject Saul as king of Israel?
questions.explanation: Saul disobeyed God by offering an unlawful sacrifice and not completely destroying the Amalekites (1 Samuel 15:22-23).

questions.text: Who killed Goliath the Philistine giant?
questions.explanation: David killed Goliath with a stone from his sling (1 Samuel 17:49).

questions.text: What weapon did David use to fight Goliath?
questions.explanation: David used a sling and a stone to defeat Goliath (1 Samuel 17:40).

questions.text: Which king of Israel was described as a man after God's own heart?
questions.explanation: David was described as a man after God's own heart (1 Samuel 13:14).

questions.text: What was the name of David's most notorious sin?
options: Murder of Uriah and adultery with Bathsheba
questions.explanation: David committed adultery with Bathsheba and arranged the death of her husband Uriah (2 Samuel 11).

questions.text: Who was the prophet that confronted David about his sin with Bathsheba?
questions.explanation: Nathan the prophet confronted David with a parable about his sin (2 Samuel 12:1-14).

questions.text: What was Solomon famous for requesting from God?
questions.explanation: Solomon asked God for wisdom and understanding to govern Israel (1 Kings 3:9-12).

questions.text: What great structure did Solomon build for God in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Solomon built the Temple in Jerusalem as a house for the Ark of the Covenant (1 Kings 6).

questions.text: How many years did it take Solomon to build the Temple?
questions.explanation: It took Solomon seven years to build the Temple (1 Kings 6:38).

questions.text: What caused the kingdom of Israel to split after Solomon's death?
options: Rehoboam's foolish answer to the people
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's harsh reply caused ten tribes to break away and form the northern kingdom (1 Kings 12:13-16).

questions.text: Who was the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel?
questions.explanation: Jeroboam became the first king of the northern kingdom after the split (1 Kings 12:20).

questions.text: On which mountain did Elijah contest with the prophets of Baal?
questions.explanation: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:20).

questions.text: What miracle did Elijah perform on Mount Carmel to prove God's power?
options: Called fire from heaven to consume the sacrifice
questions.explanation: Elijah called fire from heaven which consumed the soaked sacrifice on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:38).

questions.text: According to the Bible, how did the prophet Elijah depart and go to heaven?
questions.explanation: Elijah was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire (2 Kings 2:11).

questions.text: Who succeeded Elijah as a prophet in Israel?
questions.explanation: Elisha succeeded Elijah and received a double portion of his spirit (2 Kings 2:9).

questions.text: What did Naaman the Syrian need to do to be healed of leprosy?
options: Wash seven times in the Jordan River
questions.explanation: Elisha told Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan River to be healed (2 Kings 5:10).

questions.text: Which wicked queen of Israel promoted Baal worship?
questions.explanation: Queen Jezebel promoted Baal worship and persecuted the prophets of God (1 Kings 18:4).

questions.text: What happened to the sons of the prophet who lied about Elijah?
questions.explanation: The sons of the prophet who lied were killed by a lion as God's judgment (1 Kings 20:35-36).

questions.text: Which prophet prophesied that a virgin would conceive and bear a son?
questions.explanation: Isaiah prophesied: 'A virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel' (Isaiah 7:14).

questions.text: What title did Isaiah give to the coming Messiah in Isaiah 9:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah called the Messiah 'Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace' (Isaiah 9:6).

questions.text: To which city was Jeremiah called to prophesy?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was called to prophesy to Jerusalem and Judah before the Babylonian exile (Jeremiah 1:2).

questions.text: Why was Jeremiah called the 'weeping prophet'?
options: He wept at his own suffering
He wept over Jerusalem's coming destruction
He wept at the Temple's dedication
questions.explanation: Jeremiah wept over the sins of Judah and the coming destruction of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 9:1).

questions.text: What did God command Jeremiah to do that symbolized Judah's bondage?
options: Buy a clay jar and break it
questions.explanation: God told Jeremiah to buy a clay jar and break it to symbolize the coming destruction of Judah (Jeremiah 19:1-2).

questions.text: What did the potter and clay symbolize in Jeremiah's vision?
options: God's sovereign right to shape Israel
questions.explanation: As the potter shapes clay, God has the sovereign right to shape or reshape the nation of Israel (Jeremiah 18:6).

questions.text: Which prophet used the metaphor of a husband who would punish an unfaithful wife?
questions.explanation: Hosea's marriage to Gomer symbolized God's faithful love for unfaithful Israel (Hosea 1:2).

questions.text: Who was the wife of Hosea that represented unfaithful Israel?
questions.explanation: Gomer was Hosea's unfaithful wife who symbolized Israel's idolatry (Hosea 1:3).

questions.text: What did Hosea say about God's love for Israel?
options: It was like the love of a faithful husband
questions.explanation: Hosea portrayed God's love as that of a faithful husband pursuing his unfaithful wife (Hosea 2:14-20).

questions.text: Which prophet condemned social injustice and exploitation of the poor?
questions.explanation: Amos strongly condemned social injustice, oppression of the poor, and corrupt worship (Amos 2:6-7).

questions.text: What was Amos's profession before becoming a prophet?
options: Shepherd and dresser of sycamore trees
questions.explanation: Amos was a shepherd and dresser of sycamore trees before God called him to prophesy (Amos 7:14).

questions.text: What did Amos say about justice and righteousness?
options: Let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream
Justice is only for the rich
Justice will come only at the end of time
questions.explanation: Amos called for justice and righteousness to flow abundantly (Amos 5:24).

questions.text: Which prophet said, 'What does the Lord require of you but to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with your God?'
questions.explanation: Micah summarized God's requirements: justice, mercy, and humility (Micah 6:8).

questions.text: According to the Bible, which town or region was the prophet Micah from?
questions.explanation: Micah was from Moresheth in the land of Judah (Micah 1:1).

questions.text: What vision did Ezekiel see by the river Chebar?
options: Four living creatures and a wheels-within-wheels chariot
questions.explanation: Ezekiel saw a glorious vision of God's throne chariot with four living creatures and interlocking wheels (Ezekiel 1).

questions.text: What did the valley of dry bones vision symbolize?
options: The resurrection of Israel from exile
questions.explanation: The dry bones coming to life symbolized God's power to restore Israel from exile (Ezekiel 37:11).

questions.text: Which prophet was thrown into a cistern for prophesying the fall of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was thrown into a muddy cistern because of his unpopular prophecies (Jeremiah 38:6).

questions.text: Who was taken into exile in Babylon and interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dream?
questions.explanation: Daniel interpreted King Nebuchadnezzar's dream while in exile in Babylon (Daniel 2).

questions.text: Who were the three friends of Daniel thrown into the fiery furnace?
questions.explanation: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (also known as Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah) were thrown into the furnace (Daniel 3).

questions.text: Why were Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego thrown into the fiery furnace?
options: They refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image
They tried to escape from Babylon
questions.explanation: They refused to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image, remaining faithful to God (Daniel 3:16-18).

questions.text: Who threw Daniel into the lions' den?
questions.explanation: King Darius was tricked by jealous officials into throwing Daniel into the lions' den (Daniel 6).

questions.text: Which book of the Bible contains the story of Jonah?
questions.explanation: The Book of Jonah records Jonah's mission to Nineveh.

questions.text: What did Jonah try to do when God called him to go to Nineveh?
options: He tried to flee in the opposite direction
questions.explanation: Jonah tried to flee from God's presence by sailing to Tarshish (Jonah 1:3).

questions.text: What swallowed Jonah when he was thrown into the sea?
questions.explanation: God prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah (Jonah 1:17).

questions.text: What was the preaching theme of Jonah in Nineveh?
options: Forty more days and Nineveh will be overthrown
Believe in the one true God
questions.explanation: Jonah proclaimed that Nineveh would be overthrown in forty days (Jonah 3:4).

questions.text: Why was Jonah angry when Nineveh repented?
options: He knew God was gracious and would relent
questions.explanation: Jonah was angry because he knew God's compassionate nature and would relent from destroying Nineveh (Jonah 4:2).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about loving one's enemies?
options: Pray for those who persecute you
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded: 'Pray for those who persecute you' (Matthew 5:44).

questions.text: In which town was Jesus Christ born according to the Bible?
questions.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem (Luke 2:4-7).

questions.text: Who was the mother of jesus and what was their role in history?
questions.explanation: Mary was the mother of Jesus, conceived by the Holy Spirit (Luke 1:26-35).

questions.text: What was the name of Jesus' earthly father?
questions.explanation: Joseph was the earthly father of Jesus, a carpenter from Nazareth (Matthew 1:18-20).

questions.text: Which king ordered the killing of baby boys in Bethlehem?
questions.explanation: Herod the Great ordered the massacre of infants in Bethlehem (Matthew 2:16).

questions.text: Who were the wise men that visited baby Jesus?
questions.explanation: Magi from the East followed a star to visit the newborn king (Matthew 2:1-2).

questions.text: How many wise men visited Jesus according to tradition?
questions.explanation: Tradition holds there were three wise men, corresponding to three gifts (Matthew 2:11).

questions.text: At which place was Jesus Christ baptized?
questions.explanation: Jesus was baptized by John in the River Jordan (Matthew 3:13-16).

questions.text: Who baptized Jesus Christ in the River Jordan?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the River Jordan (Matthew 3:13-14).

questions.text: What happened when Jesus was baptized?
options: The heavens opened and the Spirit descended like a dove
questions.explanation: The heavens opened, the Spirit descended like a dove, and a voice from heaven spoke (Matthew 3:16-17).

questions.text: Where was Jesus tempted by the devil after his baptism?
options: In the wilderness for forty days
questions.explanation: Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted for forty days (Matthew 4:1-2).

questions.text: How did Jesus respond to Satan's temptation to turn stones into bread?
options: He turned the stones to bread
questions.explanation: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 8:3: 'Man shall not live by bread alone' (Matthew 4:4).

questions.text: What was the first miracle Jesus performed?
options: Turning water into wine at Cana
questions.explanation: Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding in Cana of Galilee (John 2:1-11).

questions.text: In which town did Jesus perform his first miracle?
questions.explanation: The first miracle was at a wedding feast in Cana of Galilee (John 2:1).

questions.text: What did Jesus say was the greatest commandment?
options: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind
questions.explanation: Jesus said the greatest commandment is to love God with all your heart, soul, and mind (Matthew 22:37-38).

questions.text: What was the second greatest commandment according to Jesus?
options: You shall have no other gods
questions.explanation: The second greatest commandment is to love your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:39).

questions.text: On which mountain did Jesus deliver the Sermon on the Mount?
options: The traditional site is the Mount of Beatitudes
questions.explanation: The Sermon on the Mount was delivered on a mountainside in Galilee (Matthew 5:1-2).

questions.text: Which Beatitude mentions inheriting the earth?
options: Blessed are the poor in spirit
questions.explanation: 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth' (Matthew 5:5).

questions.text: Who did Jesus call the salt of the earth?
questions.explanation: Jesus called his disciples the salt of the earth (Matthew 5:13).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about judging others?
options: Do not judge, or you will be judged
questions.explanation: Jesus taught: 'Do not judge, or you too will be judged' (Matthew 7:1).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about the narrow gate?
options: It is only for the rich
It is the gate for animals
questions.explanation: Jesus said: 'Small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it' (Matthew 7:14).

questions.text: How did Jesus feed a crowd of five thousand people?
options: With five loaves and two fish
With bread bought from the market
With fish caught from the sea
questions.explanation: Jesus multiplied five loaves and two fish to feed five thousand (John 6:9-13).

questions.text: What did Jesus do when he saw the crowd was like sheep without a shepherd?
options: He had compassion and taught them
He told them to go away
He sent them to the priests
questions.explanation: Jesus had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he taught them (Mark 6:34).

questions.text: What was the seed in Jesus' parable of the sower that fell on good soil?
options: Those who hear and produce a crop
Those who hear but fall away
Those who never hear the word
Those who hear and become anxious
questions.explanation: The seed on good soil represents those who hear the word, understand it, and produce a harvest (Matthew 13:23).

questions.text: What does the mustard seed represent in Jesus' parable?
options: Small beginnings leading to great growth
questions.explanation: The mustard seed, though the smallest seed, grows into the largest garden plant, symbolizing the growth of God's kingdom (Matthew 13:31-32).

questions.text: In the parable of the prodigal son, what did the younger son ask for?
questions.explanation: The younger son asked for his share of the father's estate (Luke 15:12).

questions.text: How did the father respond when the prodigal son returned home?
options: He ran, embraced, and kissed him
He sent him away to work
questions.explanation: The father saw him, ran to him, embraced him, and kissed him (Luke 15:20).

questions.text: What is the main lesson of the parable of the Good Samaritan?
options: Show mercy and love to anyone in need
questions.explanation: The Good Samaritan teaches us to love and show mercy to anyone in need, regardless of their background (Luke 10:30-37).

questions.text: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who passed by the wounded man first?
questions.explanation: A priest passed by first without helping (Luke 10:31).

questions.text: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who finally helped the wounded man?
questions.explanation: A Samaritan stopped, bandaged the man's wounds, and took care of him (Luke 10:33-34).

questions.text: What did Jesus teach about the lost sheep?
options: That a shepherd forgets lost sheep
That God rejoices more over one repentant sinner than ninety-nine who don't repent
That there are no lost sheep
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:7).

questions.text: To which place did Jesus Christ often go to pray according to the Gospels?
questions.explanation: Jesus often withdrew to lonely places and mountains to pray (Luke 5:16).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about storing treasures on earth?
options: It is wise to store earthly treasures
Do not store up treasures on earth where moth and rust destroy
Treasures on earth guarantee eternal life
questions.explanation: Jesus taught: 'Do not store up treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy' (Matthew 6:19).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about worrying about tomorrow?
options: Do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself
You should always plan for the worst
Worrying is a sign of faith
questions.explanation: Jesus said: 'Do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself' (Matthew 6:34).

questions.text: What did Jesus say about the beam and the speck in one's eye?
options: Remove the beam from your own eye before removing the speck from another's
Leave the speck for God to remove
questions.explanation: Jesus told his followers to remove the beam from their own eye before addressing the speck in another's (Matthew 7:5).

questions.text: Where did Jesus go when he was twelve years old?
questions.explanation: At twelve, Jesus was found in the Temple in Jerusalem, sitting among the teachers (Luke 2:46).

questions.text: Who did Jesus raise from the dead at Bethany?
questions.explanation: Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead after four days in the tomb (John 11:38-44).

questions.text: How many days was Lazarus dead before Jesus raised him?
questions.explanation: Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days before Jesus came (John 11:39).

questions.text: What did Jesus say to raise Lazarus from the tomb?
questions.explanation: Jesus called out: 'Lazarus, come forth!' and the dead man came out (John 11:43-44).

questions.text: What did Jesus do when he entered the Temple and saw the money changers?
options: He drove them out and overturned their tables
questions.explanation: Jesus made a whip, drove out the money changers, and overturned their tables (John 2:15).

questions.text: What was Jesus' response when asked about paying taxes to Caesar?
options: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's
questions.explanation: Jesus said: 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's' (Mark 12:17).

questions.text: Who asked Jesus the question about paying taxes to Caesar?
questions.explanation: A Pharisee and a Herodian came together to test Jesus with this question (Mark 12:13).

questions.text: In the parable of the ten virgins, what were the five foolish virgins lacking?
questions.explanation: The five foolish virgins did not bring extra oil for their lamps (Matthew 25:3).

questions.text: What does oil represent in the parable of the ten virgins?
questions.explanation: Oil represents spiritual preparedness and readiness for Christ's return.

questions.text: What happened to the talents of the servant who buried his one talent?
options: His talent was taken away and given to another
questions.explanation: His talent was taken and given to the servant who had ten (Matthew 25:28).

questions.text: What does the parable of the talents teach?
options: We should use God's gifts wisely and productively
Talents are only for the poor
questions.explanation: The parable teaches that we should be faithful and productive with what God has given us (Matthew 25:14-30).

questions.text: On which night did Jesus institute the Last Supper?
options: The night before his crucifixion, during Passover
questions.explanation: Jesus instituted the Last Supper on the night before his crucifixion, during the Passover meal (Luke 22:14-20).

questions.text: What did Jesus take at the Last Supper and say represented his body?
questions.explanation: Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and said: 'This is my body' (Luke 22:19).

questions.text: Who betrayed Jesus to the chief priests?
questions.explanation: Judas Iscariot agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:14-16).

questions.text: How much did Judas receive for betraying Jesus?
questions.explanation: Judas agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:15).

questions.text: What was the sign by which Judas identified Jesus to the soldiers?
questions.explanation: Judas identified Jesus by greeting him with a kiss (Matthew 26:48-49).

questions.text: Where did Jesus pray before his arrest?
questions.explanation: Jesus prayed in the Garden of Gethsemane before his arrest (Matthew 26:36).

questions.text: What did Jesus ask his Father three times in Gethsemane?
options: To take the cup of suffering away from him
questions.explanation: Jesus prayed three times: 'Father, if it is possible, may this cup be taken from me' (Matthew 26:39).

questions.text: What did Jesus say at the end of his prayer in Gethsemane?
options: Not my will, but yours be done
questions.explanation: Jesus submitted to God's will: 'Not my will, but yours be done' (Luke 22:42).

questions.text: Who denied knowing Jesus three times?
questions.explanation: Peter denied knowing Jesus three times before the rooster crowed (Matthew 26:69-75).

questions.text: What bird crowed after Peter denied Jesus the third time?
questions.explanation: A rooster crowed immediately after Peter denied Jesus the third time (Matthew 26:74).

questions.text: Who was the Roman governor who sentenced Jesus to crucifixion?
questions.explanation: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea, sentenced Jesus to crucifixion (Matthew 27:24-26).

questions.text: What did Pilate wash his hands to symbolize?
options: He was innocent of Jesus' blood
questions.explanation: Pilate washed his hands to show he was innocent of Jesus' blood (Matthew 27:24).

questions.text: What was written on the cross above Jesus' head?
questions.explanation: Pilate ordered the inscription: 'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews' (John 19:19).

questions.text: What did Jesus say while hanging on the cross about forgiveness?
options: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing
There is no forgiveness for them
questions.explanation: Jesus prayed: 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing' (Luke 23:34).

questions.text: Which criminal crucified with Jesus asked to be remembered in his kingdom?
options: The one on the right (the penitent thief)
questions.explanation: The penitent thief on Jesus' right asked to be remembered in his kingdom (Luke 23:42).

questions.text: What did Jesus say to the penitent thief on the cross?
options: Today you will be with me in paradise
questions.explanation: Jesus promised: 'Today you will be with me in paradise' (Luke 23:43).

questions.text: What did Jesus cry out just before he died on the cross?
options: My God, why have you forsaken me?
Father, into your hands I commit my spirit
All of the above were spoken before his death
questions.explanation: Jesus spoke several things including 'It is finished' and 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit' (John 19:30, Luke 23:46).

questions.text: Where was Jesus buried after his death?
options: In a new tomb cut out of rock in a garden
At the bottom of the sea
questions.explanation: Jesus was buried in a new tomb belonging to Joseph of Arimathea, cut out of rock (Matthew 27:59-60).

questions.text: Who rolled away the stone from Jesus' tomb?
questions.explanation: An angel of the Lord came down from heaven and rolled away the stone (Matthew 28:2).

questions.text: Who were the first people to discover that Jesus had risen?
options: The women who came to the tomb early in the morning
questions.explanation: Women who came to anoint Jesus' body early on the first day of the week found the tomb empty (Mark 16:2-4).

questions.text: What did the angel tell the women at Jesus' empty tomb?
options: He is not here; he has risen
questions.explanation: The angel said: 'He is not here; he has risen, just as he said' (Matthew 28:6).

questions.text: How many days did Jesus remain on earth after his resurrection before ascending?
questions.explanation: Jesus appeared to his disciples over forty days before ascending to heaven (Acts 1:3).

questions.text: From where did Jesus ascend into heaven?
questions.explanation: Jesus ascended from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:12).

questions.text: What did Jesus promise to send to his disciples after his ascension?
questions.explanation: Jesus promised to send the Holy Spirit to be with and guide his disciples (John 14:26).

questions.text: On which day did the Holy Spirit descend on the disciples at Pentecost?
options: The first day of the week
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit descended on the Day of Pentecost, fifty days after the Passover (Acts 2:1).

questions.text: What appeared over each disciple's head at Pentecost?
questions.explanation: Tongues of fire appeared and rested on each of them (Acts 2:3).

questions.text: What gift did the disciples receive at Pentecost that enabled them to speak in other languages?
options: The gift of tongues (speaking in other languages)
questions.explanation: They were filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking in other languages (Acts 2:4).

questions.text: How many people were added to the church on the Day of Pentecost?
questions.explanation: About three thousand were added to their number that day (Acts 2:41).

questions.text: Who preached the first sermon at Pentecost?
questions.explanation: Peter stood up with the eleven and preached the first Christian sermon (Acts 2:14).

questions.text: What did Peter tell the crowd to do in response to his Pentecost sermon?
options: Repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Peter told them to repent and be baptized for the forgiveness of sins (Acts 2:38).

questions.text: What did the early Christians practice regarding their possessions?
questions.explanation: The early believers shared everything they had and sold possessions to give to those in need (Acts 2:44-45).

questions.text: Who was the first Christian martyr mentioned in Acts?
questions.explanation: Stephen was stoned to death and is considered the first Christian martyr (Acts 7:54-60).

questions.text: What did Stephen see as he was being stoned?
options: The heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand
questions.explanation: Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, saw heaven open and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand (Acts 7:55-56).

questions.text: Who consented to Stephen's execution by holding the garments?
questions.explanation: Saul (later Paul) approved of Stephen's execution and guarded the coats (Acts 7:58).

questions.text: On which road was Saul traveling when he encountered the risen Christ?
questions.explanation: Saul was on the road to Damascus when a light from heaven blinded him and he heard Jesus' voice (Acts 9:3).

questions.text: What did Saul do for three days after his encounter with Christ on the Damascus road?
options: He fasted and could not see
questions.explanation: Saul was blind and did not eat or drink for three days (Acts 9:9).

questions.text: Who was sent by God to restore Saul's sight?
questions.explanation: God sent Ananias to lay hands on Saul and restore his sight (Acts 9:17-18).

questions.text: What was Saul's name changed to after his conversion?
questions.explanation: Saul became known as Paul, his Roman name, after his conversion (Acts 13:9).

questions.text: Which disciple was known for doubting the resurrection until he saw Jesus' wounds?
questions.explanation: Thomas doubted until he saw and touched Jesus' wounds (John 20:24-29).

questions.text: What did Jesus say to Thomas when he believed?
options: Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed
You are the strongest of my disciples
questions.explanation: Jesus said: 'Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed' (John 20:29).

questions.text: How many fish did the disciples catch when Jesus told them to cast their net on the right side?
questions.explanation: They caught one hundred and fifty-three large fish (John 21:11).

questions.text: What three times did Jesus ask Peter, 'Do you love me?' and what did he commission Peter to do?
options: Feed my lambs, tend my sheep, feed my sheep
Preach the word, heal the sick, cast out demons
Build my church, lead my people, spread my gospel
Love God, love your neighbor, love yourself
questions.explanation: Jesus asked Peter three times if he loved him and told him to feed his lambs, tend his sheep, and feed his sheep (John 21:15-17).

questions.text: What was the Great Commission Jesus gave to his disciples?
options: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded: 'Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit' (Matthew 28:19-20).

questions.text: Who was the first person Paul converted on his missionary journeys?
questions.explanation: Lydia from Thyatira was the first European convert, baptized along with her household (Acts 16:14-15).

questions.text: Where were Paul and Silas imprisoned and what happened at midnight?
options: They sang hymns and an earthquake shook the prison
They were released by the jailer
questions.explanation: Paul and Silas prayed and sang hymns, and God sent an earthquake that opened the prison doors (Acts 16:25-26).

questions.text: What happened to the Philippian jailer when the prison doors flew open?
options: He was about to kill himself but was stopped by Paul
questions.explanation: The jailer was about to kill himself thinking the prisoners had escaped, but Paul stopped him (Acts 16:27-28).

questions.text: What did Paul say was the greatest Christian virtue in 1 Corinthians 13?
questions.explanation: Paul wrote that love is the greatest virtue, greater than faith and hope (1 Corinthians 13:13).

questions.text: How does 1 Corinthians 13 describe love?
questions.explanation: 'Love is patient, love is kind' (1 Corinthians 13:4).

questions.text: What does Paul say love does NOT do in 1 Corinthians 13?
options: It does not rejoice in the truth
It does not envy or boast
questions.explanation: Paul lists many things love does not do: envy, boast, are not proud, not self-seeking, not easily angered (1 Corinthians 13:4-5).

questions.text: In Paul's letter to the Romans, what does he say about faith without works?
options: It is the only thing needed
questions.explanation: James writes that faith without works is dead (James 2:26). Paul emphasizes that we are justified by faith.

questions.text: According to Paul, how are people saved?
options: By grace through faith, not by works
By making sacrifices at the Temple
questions.explanation: Paul taught that we are saved by grace through faith, not by works of the law (Ephesians 2:8-9).

questions.text: What did Paul describe as the 'armor of God'?
options: Spiritual armor including truth, righteousness, faith, and the word of God
questions.explanation: Paul described spiritual armor: belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shield of faith, helmet of salvation, sword of the Spirit (Ephesians 6:10-18).

questions.text: According to Paul’s letters, what was the nature of ‘the thorn in the flesh’?
options: The exact nature is not clearly stated in Scripture
questions.explanation: The exact nature of Paul's thorn in the flesh is not specified in Scripture (2 Corinthians 12:7).

questions.text: What did God say to Paul about his thorn in the flesh?
options: My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness
It will go away in time
questions.explanation: God replied: 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness' (2 Corinthians 12:9).

questions.text: What fruit of the Spirit does Paul list in Galatians 5?
options: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control
questions.explanation: Paul listed nine fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22-23.

questions.text: How many fruit of the Spirit does Paul list in Galatians 5:22-23?
questions.explanation: Paul lists nine fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.

questions.text: What did Paul say about the unity of the body of Christ in 1 Corinthians 12?
options: If one part suffers, all suffer together; if one part is honored, all rejoice
questions.explanation: Paul taught that all parts of Christ's body are interconnected and share in each other's sufferings and joys (1 Corinthians 12:26).

questions.text: What did Paul call himself before his conversion?
questions.explanation: Paul called himself the chief of sinners, having persecuted the church (1 Timothy 1:15).

questions.text: What did Paul say in Philippians 4:13?
options: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me
I am the weakest of all
questions.explanation: 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' (Philippians 4:13).

questions.text: Which letter did Paul write to a slave owner about the runaway slave Onesimus?
questions.explanation: Paul wrote to Philemon urging him to receive the runaway slave Onesimus as a brother in Christ (Philemon 1:8-16).

questions.text: What did Paul urge Philemon to do with Onesimus?
options: Send him back as a slave
Receive him no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother
questions.explanation: Paul urged Philemon to receive Onesimus as a beloved brother in Christ (Philemon 1:16).

questions.text: In which city was Paul shipwrecked on his way to Rome?
questions.explanation: Paul was shipwrecked on the island of Malta (Acts 28:1).

questions.text: What happened to the viper that bit Paul on Malta?
options: He shook it off into the fire and suffered no harm
He became ill for a week
questions.explanation: Paul shook the viper into the fire and was unharmed, stunning the islanders (Acts 28:3-6).

questions.text: What does Paul teach about Christian love in Romans 12?
options: Love only those who love you
Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse
questions.explanation: Paul taught: 'Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse' (Romans 12:14).

questions.text: What does Paul say about revenge in Romans 12?
options: Do not repay anyone evil for evil; leave room for God's wrath
Revenge is God's gift to us
questions.explanation: Paul wrote: 'Do not repay anyone evil for evil... Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God's wrath' (Romans 12:17-19).

questions.text: What did Paul say about submission to governing authorities in Romans 13?
options: Everyone must submit to governing authorities
questions.explanation: Paul taught that governing authorities are established by God and we should submit to them (Romans 13:1).

questions.text: In which city did Paul deliver the famous speech at the Areopagus?
questions.explanation: Paul preached at the Areopagus in Athens, addressing the altar to an unknown god (Acts 17:22-31).

questions.text: What did Paul say about God at the Areopagus in Athens?
options: The God who made the world does not live in temples made by human hands
God is unknown and cannot be found
God only cares about the rich
questions.explanation: Paul declared that the God who made the world does not live in temples built by human hands (Acts 17:24).

questions.text: What did Paul preach at the Areopagus about all people?
options: From one man God made all nations to live on the earth
questions.explanation: Paul said: 'From one man he made all the nations' (Acts 17:26).

questions.text: What is Paul's teaching on forgiveness in Colossians 3?
options: Bear with each other and forgive one another
Forgiveness is only for God to give
questions.explanation: Paul wrote: 'Bear with each other and forgive one another if any of you has a grievance' (Colossians 3:13).

questions.text: What does Paul teach about the second coming of Christ in 1 Thessalonians 4?
options: The dead in Christ will rise first, then those who are alive will be caught up together
Only the righteous will see him
He will return silently and secretly
questions.explanation: Paul taught that the dead in Christ will rise first, then those who are alive will be caught up together with them (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17).

questions.text: What does Paul teach about prayer in 1 Thessalonians 5?
questions.explanation: Paul commanded: 'Pray without ceasing' (1 Thessalonians 5:17).

questions.text: What did Paul say about the resurrection of the dead in 1 Corinthians 15?
options: If Christ has not been raised, our faith is futile
questions.explanation: Paul argued: 'If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile' (1 Corinthians 15:17).

questions.text: What does Paul compare Christ's return to in 1 Corinthians 15?
questions.explanation: Paul and other writers compare Christ's sudden return to a thief coming in the night (1 Thessalonians 5:2).

questions.text: According to James, what is faith without works?
questions.explanation: James wrote: 'Faith without works is dead' (James 2:26).

questions.text: What does James say about the tongue?
options: It is a small member but boasts of great things and sets the whole course of life on fire
questions.explanation: James compared the tongue to a small rudder that steers a large ship, saying it can corrupt the whole person (James 3:5-6).

questions.text: What does James say about the power of prayer?
options: The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective
questions.explanation: James wrote: 'The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective' (James 5:16).

questions.text: According to Peter, what is our living hope through the resurrection of Jesus?
options: An inheritance that can never perish, spoil, or fade
questions.explanation: Peter wrote that through Christ we have an inheritance kept in heaven that can never perish, spoil, or fade (1 Peter 1:4).

questions.text: According to the first letter of John, what does Scripture reveal about the nature of God?
options: God is only for the wealthy
questions.explanation: John wrote: 'God is love' (1 John 4:8).

questions.text: According to 1 John 4, how can we know God abides in us?
options: By the Spirit he gave us
questions.explanation: John wrote: 'This is how we know that he lives in us: We know it by the Spirit he gave us' (1 John 4:13).

questions.text: What does John say we must do if we claim to love God but hate our brother?
options: We are liars and the truth is not in us
Love of God is more important
questions.explanation: John wrote: 'Whoever claims to love God yet hates a brother or sister is a liar' (1 John 4:20).

questions.text: In Revelation, what does Jesus promise to those who overcome?
options: They will sit with him on his throne
They will rule the world politically
questions.explanation: Jesus promised: 'The one who conquers... will sit with me on my throne' (Revelation 3:21).

questions.text: What does Revelation 21:1 describe as the new creation?
options: A new universe and a new earth
A new Garden of Eden on earth
questions.explanation: John saw 'a new heaven and a new earth' (Revelation 21:1).
